newsitem.title: USA: ADM unfazed by USDA food contract review.
newsitem.headline: ADM unfazed by USDA food contract review.

text.p: An ongoing review of Archer Daniels Midland Co's government contracts by the U.S. Agriculture Department was of minimal concern to the grain processing giant, a spokeswoman for the company said.
"It would affect less than one-half of one percent of our business," said spokeswoman Karla Miller. "It's really immaterial."
She added that ADM's past dealings with the USDA were both "unprofitable and a nuisance," and were done typically as an accommodation.
USDA said this week that it was compiling a list of contracts to decide whether to bar ADM from participation in federal food programs because of ADM's guilty plea to two price-fixing charges.
The value of ADM's government contracts "would be difficult to calculate because it's such a small amount" of total sales, Miller said. ADM's sales were $13.3 billion in the year ended June 30.
